items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: James Brown was a pain in the neck. When I had to do what I had to do to show my butt with him, I did it and it was over. You go in and you do your job.

ctx.x: Well you know I can see why you would — with what you’ve said about just the groove of a song and the meaning of a song — why you would like something like Floyd Cramer. Because it’s not about technique and lots of notes, it’s just about the simplicity and nice feel.

And that’s what I had to do all my life. Learn to be simple. When I play I play simple. I am right down the middle. And I know how to go from one side to the other without a problem. I don’t have a problem. Because I’m going to be the simplest person in there. But yet I’m going to groove with it. That is part of my whole life. All my life I was taught that. I was taught that’s what you need to do, that’s what you need to focus on. You focus in on the music. You focus everything about what you have to do. And…
